question.text: The State of Lu's official chronicle, the Annals, provided the name for a "period" where the Eastern Zhou began named after two of these time periods-spring and autumn.
question.clue: To display the Emerald Buddha in Wat Phra Kaew, Rama I and Rama III constructed three sets of decorations based on these time periods, including a "rainy" example characterized by monsoons.

swap.text: This is the total number of women who have ever been Supreme Court justices, past and present.
swap.clue: Jiang Qing, Mao's final wife, was a member of a group of this number of people. Sparrows were exterminated as part of a campaign against this number of pests.

question.leadin: This event's "Down to the Countryside" Movement sent youth from cities to farms, resulting in a "lost generation." --.
question.text: Identify this movement that targeted the "four olds." The "Gang of Four" became prominent during this period that attempted to purge any remaining elements of capitalism from a certain country.
question.clue: Just before this event's beginning, a February Outline was issued by the Five Man Group as a response to an accusation that a real-life house arrest was the basis of the allegedly unpatriotic drama Hai Rui Dismissed From Office.

swap.text: This military leader of the Kuomintang led the Northern Expedition at the start of the Chinese Civil War. He later led the Republic of China's exiled government on Taiwan.
swap.clue: Earlier, this man's Northern Expedition had toppled the Beiyang government, though his later pledge to establish a second United Front was made under duress while being held by Marshal Zhang Xueliang during the Xi'an incident.

question.text: The Taiping Heavenly Kingdom was located in this city, which was the capital of the Ming dynasty before Beijing. John Rabe created a "Safety Zone" in this city in 1937.
question.clue: A contest to kill one hundred people with a sword took place in this city, which was once the site of the Porcelain Tower.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Japanese expansion before the attack on Pearl Harbor.
swap.text: The first major fighting of the war occurred in the assault on this coastal Chinese city. Peter Harmsen described this battle as the "Stalingrad of the Yangtze" because of its immense casualties.
swap.clue: A tea house is located in the center of a lake in this city located near the Yu Garden.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Chinese history in the late 19th to 20th century.
question.text: This political party was founded by Sun Yat-sen, who was succeeded by Chiang Kai-Shek. This party lost the Chinese Civil War to the Communist Party of China.
question.clue: One leader of this party adapted Henry George's philosophy to form his Three Principles of the People.

swap.text: The kingdom of Wei was founded by this man's son, Pi. This warlord won the Battle of Guandu, and served as the chancellor to the last Han emperor.
swap.clue: This man's campaign to restore the lands of the Eastern Han was halted at the Battle of Red Cliffs, where he was defeated by Liu Bei and Sun Quan ].

question.leadin: Answer the following about China's last emperor, P'u Yi.
question.text: P'u Yi lived his young life in this complex, not leaving until he was forced to in 1924. Aside from royals, the only males allowed in the inner palace were court eunuchs.
question.clue: The earth removed in the construction of the moat around this place was used to create Jingshan Hill, the place where the Chongzhen Emperor committed suicide.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Mongol khans.
swap.text: This khan expanded the Mongol Empire to its furthest extent. He launched a failed invasion of Japan and established the Yuan Dynasty in China.
swap.clue: The creation of the Phags-pa script was commissioned by this ruler, whose naval forces were outnumbered ten to one off the coast of Guangdong but still managed to win the Battle of Yamen.

question.leadin: This woman died in the Hall of Graceful Bird, probably due to arsenic poisoning.
question.text: Name this woman who dominated the Qing Dynasty for over forty years. She was the mother of the Tongzhi Emperor and the aunt of the Guangxu Emperor. Either her name or her familiar title is okay.
question.answerHtml: Cixi [or Tzu-his, or the Dowager Empress, accept in reverse order]
question.clue: Despite later supporting the "New Policies," this ruler placed the Guangxu ("gwahng-shyoo") Emperor under house arrest after he launched the Hundred Days' Reform.

swap.text: The Silla Kingdom allied with this Chinese dynasty to conquer its neighbors. This dynasty was interrupted by Wu Zetian's short-lived Zhou Dynasty.
swap.clue: This dynasty lost the battle of Talas to the Abbasids.

question.text: After passing the final Metropolitan Exam, candidates were awarded this highest and final degree. The purchasing of this degree toward the end of the Qing (ching) meant the "Imperial Scholars" who held it were no longer guaranteed the highest offices.
question.clue: Successful candidates in the civil service exams were awarded this degree title. From the reign of the Ming emperor Yingzong ("EENG-DZONG"), only holders of this title were permitted into the Hanlin Academy.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the career of the Chinese polymath Zhang Heng.
swap.text: Zhang invented an early one of these devices, which consisted of a jar with eight dragon heads surrounded by frogs. Historians theorize a pendulum would knock a ball out into a frog mouth when the device was activated.
swap.answerHtml: seismometer [or seismograph; prompt on descriptions like earthquake detectors and such]

question.text: Chu's Pei County was the birthplace of this man, who struggled with Xiang Yu after Xiang inflicted several defeats on Qin forces. This man, who supposedly bore resemblance to a dragon, defeated Xiang Yu at the battle of Gaixia and founded a new line of rulers.
question.clue: Late in life, he favored Lady Qi as concubine, though she was murdered by his Empress afer his death.

swap.text: The Khitan people ruled this dynasty of northern China that was paid off by the Song dynasty before the northern Jurchen people overthrew this dynasty to establish the Jin dynasty.
swap.clue: After the demise of this dynasty, Yelu Dashi fled to Central Asia and established a successor state.

question.text: A group of Muslim mercenaries from Bukhara were settled near this city by Emperor Shenzhong of Song, whose capital was here. This city fell to Jurchen invaders in 1127.
question.clue: The scroll painting Along the River During the Qingming Festival likely depicts the splendor of this capital city before its final two emperors, Qinzong ("cheen-dzong") and Huizong ("hway-dzong"), were captured in the Jingkang Incident.

swap.leadin: During its Eastern phase, this dynasty granted tax exemptions to resettled migrants from north China called qiaoren.
swap.text: Name this dynasty ruled by the Sima family, whose earlier Western phase began with its reunification of China in 280 CE and ended following multiple civil wars named for Eight Princes and Five Barbarians.
swap.clue: Its forces expelled the ruler Yelu Dashi to the west, where he founded the Kara-Khitan Khanate with surviving forces of the Liao dynasty.

question.text: The Tang Dynasty came to an end after a peasant uprising started by this man and Wang Xianzhi. He captured Changan but was betrayed by his general Zhu Wen, who in turn deposed the last Tang emperor.

swap.text: Peaceful "wo lei fei" in Hong Kong often participate in protests by performing this action. A controversial law passed in June 2020 made it a crime to lodge "insults" when this action was taking place in Hong Kong.
swap.answerHtml: singing [accept answers like singing the official or unofficial national anthem; accept playing a national anthem]
swap.clue: The Baltic countries gained independence from the Soviet Union in a "revolution" named for this action. That revolution named for this action included the formation of a human chain across all three countries.
